2da1673abd86f2e2.prompt:
Choose the domain packs this app needs from the index below. Match the app's purpose to the pack's purpose and pick line. Include a matching domain even when core components cover some screens. Choose [] only for a core-only app with no matching domain. Use the best matching pack for each independently requested job. Do not add another pack for details the chosen pack already covers.

- assistant: Conversations with an AI: streaming answers and code, cited sources, tool traces, generated artifacts, starter prompts and voice mode. Pick: Use assistant alone for an AI chat that accepts notes and generates guides or other artifacts. Add workspace only for independent file sharing or editing, and media only for a separately managed reading library. Not human chat (comms) or graded quizzes (learning).
- auto: Cars and EVs: a vehicle garage, remote controls, mileage-based maintenance, OBD diagnostics, charging and fill-ups, parking meters, and used-car listings with VIN reports. Pick: Pick for operating, maintaining, charging, parking or shopping for vehicles. A used-car shortlist with VIN reports is auto alone, not an owned-asset catalog (inventory). Not turn-by-turn guidance (navigation), home automation (home), or a map of venues or stations (places).
- beauty: Personal skincare and haircare routines, opened-product shelf life, ingredient and skin-type checks, beauty profiles and saved shade lookbooks. Pick: Use for managing a personal beauty regimen. Not buying products (commerce), booking salon visits (booking), or virtual AR try-on (core).
- booking: Offer services and book appointments, classes and free start times. Pick: Booking time with someone: appointments, classes, slots and class waitlists. Booking alone covers clients booking a provider's appointments or studio classes; clients, providers, paid services and class groups do not imply customers, team, commerce, events or community. Add another pack only for an explicitly requested separate job. Not selling goods (commerce). Reply only with a valid JSON array of pack ids, never an object, invented app name or explanation.
- books: Keeping a small business's books: record money received and spent, retain receipts, separate business costs from owner withdrawals, and understand a period's profit and tax provision. The default is local cash-basis bookkeeping for one business, not banking, certified accounts or automatic tax filing. Pick: A small business's own accounts: income, expenses, profit, tax set aside. Not personal money (money), client invoices (customers), or selling goods (commerce)
- comics: Webtoons and manga: read sequential panels, follow series on a shelf, see weekly release calendars and unlock serialized chapters with coins or wait timers. Pick: Use for sequential visual storytelling and chapter gates. Not prose books or audio (media), or simply showing standalone illustrations (core).
- commerce: Goods on offer, a basket, an order and its progress, from both sides: the buyer browsing and ordering, and the seller seeing orders come in, moving them on and keeping products up to date. It covers small sellers (a bakery taking pre-orders, a market stall, a maker selling prints). Taking payment is always a service part. Pick: Selling things for money: a shop, a bakery, a stall. Not booking time (booking)
- comms: Direct and workplace communication across chat and email threads, server channels, contacts, and voice or video calls. Pick: Multi-thread inboxes, channel navigation, call lobbies, voicemail and T9 dialing. Not one simple conversation (core), public feeds (social), club governance (community), or service tickets (requests).
- community: The continuing work of a member-run group: who belongs and can vote, subscriptions collected by the treasurer, motions decided under the group's rules, contributions people claim, and the agreed record of decisions and actions. Notices use the core; this pack adds governance, not another social feed. Pick: A club, association or neighbourhood group run by its members: dues, notices, votes, sign-ups, minutes. Member subscriptions and spending votes are governance, not personal finance (money); member sign-ups are not appointments (booking). Not sharing posts (social), not organising one gathering (events), not staff shifts (team)
- curation: Collect visual inspiration in staggered pin grids, inspect sources and palettes, build shared moodboards and flatlay collages, and discover preferred styles. Pick: Use for gathering inspiration, not editing photos (studio), shopping a catalog (commerce), or tracking owned items (inventory).
- customers: Keep a business's client records, history, invoices, reviews, rewards and signed agreements. Pick: A client book: keep records about clients, such as profiles, visit history and notes, consent, agreements, client invoices, reviews and loyalty. Choose customers for a client-records job, not because another workflow has customers or records transactions. Buying goods and checking out are commerce; reserving appointments is booking. Friends sharing posts, comments and follows belong to social.
- data: The back office of a small operation: many records at once, sorted and filtered, moved through stages, changed in bulk, and summarised in charts. Any pack component allowed by the README's density rule may be dense. Pick: Running something behind the scenes: tables, boards, reports. Not personal tracking (core)
- dating: Romantic matching: relationship profiles, mutual likes, expiring match queues, compatibility, icebreakers and safety check-ins for dates. Pick: Use for finding or meeting a match, not public posts (social), ordinary direct messages (comms), or simple swipe cards (core).
- dining: Restaurant and café customer flows: dietary menus, configurable dishes, curbside or drive-through check-in, tables and walk-in queues, and diner points rewards. Pick: Use for dining out, configurable restaurant orders or a restaurant's tables and walk-in queue. Restaurant reservations and waitlists alone do not need booking or places. Not meals cooked at home (kitchen), ordinary bakery or shop pre-orders (commerce), or a business's client book (customers).
- dispatch: Independent courier or gig driver operations: go online by zone, accept timed offers, verify pickup and dropoff, and see shift payout breakdowns. Pick: Use for a worker handling live delivery jobs, not staff rosters (team), customer parcel maps (places), passenger ride tracking (navigation), or bookkeeping (books).
- events: Running one event from the organiser's side and the guest's: who is invited and coming, what they will eat, where they sit, who supplies what and what it costs, tickets and the door on the day, the gift list, and finding a date that suits everyone. Weddings, parties, reunions, fundraisers, small conferences. Pick: Organising one gathering: guests, RSVPs, seating, tickets, suppliers, gifts. Not travel (trips)
- fantasy: Fantasy leagues and player-stat contests: snake drafts, fantasy lineups, waiver bids, live fantasy matchups, prop picks, odds boards and pick slips. Pick: Use when managers draft real players into fantasy rosters or predict player outcomes. Not running a real sports league (sports), or a casual tabletop game (play).
- health: The most-asked personal app family: logging workouts set by set, taking medication on time, watching a body measurement move toward a goal, keeping several healthy habits, tracking symptoms, vitals and a menstrual cycle. Everything stays on the phone; nothing here is medical advice, and "what's real?" says so. Pick: The body: workouts, medication, measurements, symptoms, cycles. Not the mind (mind), not food (kitchen)
- hiring: Before someone joins a team, a small employer tracks openings and applicants, reviews evidence, arranges interviews and records offers. A job seeker tracks the same process from the other side. Both can keep records on one phone; this pack does not promise a job board, shared recruiting system or automatic hiring. Pick: Finding people or work: job posts, applicants, interviews, offers and your own applications. Not staff already hired (team), not clients (customers), not a generic kanban (data)
- home: The work of a home shared among the people in it: chores and whose turn it is, rewards for kids, the family's week, recurring care for pets, plants, the car and the house, a baby's feeds and sleeps, and the devices in the rooms, including set points, one-tap scenes and sensor readings. Pick: Running a household: chores, family, pets, plants, cars, the house and its devices. Not a business team (team)
- inventory: Knowing what you have, where it is, who has it, when its warranty ends and what you still want, from a garage of boxes to a small shop's stock room, a record collection or a few rental flats. For rentals it covers the listing, the lease and a single rental-repair summary only; any request workflow (queue, triage, thread, work order) belongs to the requests pack. The tenants themselves are customers. Pick: Keeping track of things owned: stock, collections, storage, loans, warranties, rentals. Not selling them (commerce)
- invest: Following money set aside for the future: what is owned, how its value changes apart from contributions, what income it pays, and how close it brings a savings target. It records investments, not advice or orders to a broker. A first showcase uses local records and dated quotes; live prices need a service. Pick: Investments over time: holdings, allocation, watchlists, performance, dividends, savings goals. Not day-to-day spending and bills (money), not a business's books (books, proposed)
- kids: Child-facing experiences for pre-readers: profile avatars, sounds and phonics, illustrated read-alongs, stickers, visual routines and parent gates. Pick: Use kids alone for a young child's icon-first experience, even when an adult unlocks settings or the child follows a visual routine. Not graded lessons (learning), parent-managed logs and screen limits (parenting), or family chore management (home).
- kitchen: Everything about food in a household: cooking from a recipe with the right amounts and timers, planning the week's meals, the shopping list that follows from it, what is in the cupboard and when it goes off, and a simple log of what was eaten. Pick: Food at home: recipes, meal plans, groceries, the pantry, food logs. Not selling food (commerce)
- learning: Learning something step by step and checking it stuck: lessons, questions with feedback, flashcards with spaced review, a path through units, results and badges, and a student's week of classes and homework. Pick: Teaching and practising: lessons, quizzes, flashcards, classes and homework. Not a team's training rota (team)
- marketplace: Peer-to-peer resale, auctions, negotiated offers, seller bundles, hosted drops and shipping labels for secondhand sellers. Pick: Use marketplace alone for private sellers' secondhand listings, bundles and auctions. Items being offered for resale do not require a stock or possessions catalog (inventory). Not a fixed-price retail storefront (commerce), used-car search (auto), or live-event ticket resale (ticketing).
- media: A library of things to read, hear or watch: articles, books, podcasts, albums, sermons, video courses. The core Player plays one recording; this pack adds what a library needs around it: the reading view, a show's page, episode lists, chapters, a player that follows the person between screens, and saved highlights. Pick: Reading, listening and watching a library. Not one recording on one screen (core Player)
- medical: Patient portal, pharmacy and clinical workflows: lab reference ranges, prescription refills and prices, telehealth, insurance coverage, care records and connected therapy summaries. No automated diagnosis. Pick: Pick for provider-facing or patient-facing clinical records or care workflows. Not personal exercise, symptom or pill tracking (health), or nonclinical client billing (customers).
- mind: Looking after how one feels: a daily check-in of mood and what affected it, a journal, naming feelings, breathing exercises, sleep, calming sounds, and the patterns that show up over weeks. It is calm by design: soft presets, no red alarms, nothing competitive. Pick: The mind: mood, journaling, feelings, breathing, sleep. Not the body (health)
- money: Personal and household money: what is in each account, where it went, what is due, who owes whom, how to clear debts, and how a holding is doing. It never moves money in a first showcase; bank links and payments are service, and "what's real?" says so. Pick: The person's own money: balances, budgets, bills, splitting costs, debts and repayment plans. Not a business's sales (commerce)
- navigation: Active routing and mobility: turn-by-turn and lane guidance, route alternatives, transit legs, road hazards, trail elevation, offline maps and passenger ride tracking. Pick: Use navigation alone to compare routes, follow turn-by-turn directions on bike or foot, or make transit transfers. A destination, stop or hazard on that route does not need places. Choose places only for a separate venue, departure-board or parcel-map workflow. Not holiday itineraries (trips) or a driver's job offers (dispatch).
- news: Follow journalism and developing stories with attributed headlines, comparisons across outlets, live blogs, breaking tickers, daily digests and publisher follows. Pick: Use for discovering and following current reporting, not personal updates (social), a personal library of already saved newsletters, books or audio (media), or an enduring encyclopedia (reference).
- paperwork: IDs, insurance, tax evidence, certificates and personal contracts, with action dates and proof files. The pack is a local filing cabinet, not a bank, travel wallet, warranty book or client-consent workflow. Its hand-drawn signature pad for personal forms does not promise legally verified e-signing. Pick: Life admin: documents, renewals, receipts, forms to sign and deadlines. Not travel documents (trips), owned things' warranties (inventory), client agreements (customers) or payments to track (money)
- parenting: Parent-facing pregnancy, pediatric growth, co-parenting and child wellbeing: gestational milestones, growth percentiles, custody swaps, child expenses, screen limits and private family albums. Pick: Use for pregnancy, growth, custody or child-specific caregiver workflows. A parent gate for settings in a child-facing app belongs to kids, not parenting. Not household chores, general family routines or a simple baby log (home), or clinical records (medical).
- perks: Multi-merchant cashback offers, verified coupon feeds and points-to-cash progress and redemption. Pick: Use when earning or redeeming offers across merchants is the app's job. Not single-store promotions (commerce), restaurant loyalty (dining), or managing one business's client rewards (customers).
- places: Real places and moving between them: a venue's card and opening hours, an address to copy or navigate to, a map with a list beside it, a delivery coming to the door, and the next departures from a stop. Maps and live data need a service. Pick: Where things are and getting there: venues, addresses, deliveries, departures. Not planning a trip (trips)
- play: Tools for playing around one phone: keep a board game's round scores, roll dice, spin for a random choice, take turns, reveal a trivia answer and split the players into teams. It supports the game at the table, not a general game engine, a sports season or a course. No wagers, prizes for money or payments. Pick: Playing a game together: round scores, dice, a spinner, turns, host-led trivia and random teams. Not league fixtures and standings (sports), not graded practice (learning), not household duties (home)
- projects: Delivering a bounded piece of work: agree what is included, break it into assigned tasks, meet milestone gates, see dependencies across dates, and record the time spent on each task. It serves one person managing their own work first; collaborators and clients do not have to use the app. Pick: Work with deliverables: projects, tasks, milestones, time spent. Not running day-to-day operations (data), not staff shifts (team)
- property: The operating view of rented homes: which independently lettable units are occupied, who owes rent for which period, who is viewing, what condition each room was in, and how meters changed. A landlord or host can keep these records on one phone; tenant accounts, automatic payments and booking-platform sync are not implied. This pack does not replace inventory's Lease or Listing. Pick: Landlord operations: rental units, dated occupancy, rent charges and receipts, viewings, inspections and meters. Use property alone for those operations. Add inventory for separately requested listings, leases or owned assets, and money for separate personal finances. Not repair and maintenance queues (requests)
- puzzles: Playable solo puzzles: five-letter word guesses with colored clues, Sudoku with pencil marks, logic and tile grids, and lifeline trivia. Pick: Choose puzzles even for one private daily word game or Sudoku. Guess distributions, streaks and daily cadence are part of the puzzle, not separate domains. Not group or host-led trivia and board games (play), or coursework and exam drills (learning).
- realestate: Home buying and apartment hunting: price-pin maps, property listings, comparison and saved alerts, mortgage affordability and arranging tours. Pick: Use for a buyer or renter searching for a home. Not operating occupied rental units (property), storing one signed lease (inventory), or everyday budgeting (money).
- reference: Read canonical or structured reference material: scripture verse lookup, study plans, parallel translations, dictionary senses and pronunciation, and cited encyclopedia articles. Pick: Use for looking up words, verses or facts. Not consuming general books or audio (media), graded study (learning), or accounting (books).
- requests: An operator takes a reported problem through triage, assigned work, updates and verified resolution. Reports can span visits, have several work orders, wait for parts or information, and reopen after a failed fix. Pick: Requests moving through a service queue: repairs, maintenance, support tickets, work orders. Not booking time (booking), not a simple repair attached to something owned (inventory), not arbitrary records on a board (data)
- rpg: Tabletop role-playing character sheets and encounters: abilities, modifiers, hit points, conditions, spell slots, dice macros, initiative and gear. Pick: Use for pen-and-paper RPG campaigns and encounters. Not standalone dice and game-night score pads (play), or real-time video games (core).
- safety: Personal safety across a trusted circle: live locations, place arrival alerts, safe-driving summaries, hold-to-send SOS and timed check-ins with escalation. Pick: Use for a person's or group's location safety. Not venue and delivery tracking (places), routing (navigation), generic household routines (home), or child screen limits (parenting).
- security: Account and connection protection: rotating 2FA codes, MFA approvals, password and passkey vaults, password generators, recovery codes, VPN controls and credential audits. Pick: Pick for securing sign-ins or connections. Not filing life-admin documents (paperwork) or checking connection speed (utilities).
- social: A small community in one app: a club, a class, a neighbourhood, friends with a shared hobby. People post, react, comment, vote, join challenges and events, and invite others. Everything here needs other people, so the pack is tier people throughout. Pick: People sharing with each other: posts, comments, follows. Not a business's clients (customers)
- sports: Amateur and grassroots sport, run by volunteers: the next match and who is available, the lineup, keeping the score live, what happened in the match, the league table and a knockout cup. It works for any sport with sides, scores and fixtures; football is the default for positions and periods. Pick: A sports team or league: fixtures, scores, standings, lineups, availability. Not a workout (health)
- stays: Shop for lodging and travel fares before booking: compare nightly prices, fare calendars, room rates, amenities and cancellation policies, and watch for price drops. Pick: Use stays alone for pre-booking fare searches and lodging shortlists. Use trips instead for keeping confirmations, packing or an itinerary. Not appointments and class slots (booking).
- studio: Structured visual creation: photo contact sheets, before-and-after wipes, filter presets, brand kits, graphic templates, AI image or video prompt desks and export queues. Pick: Use for transforming photos or producing visual assets. Not a consumption library (media), inspiration pinboards (curation), or freehand and multitrack editors (core).
- team: A small group that works together on a schedule: who is on when, who can cover a gap, hours worked, what the last shift handed over, and requests waiting for a manager. It suits cafés, salons, clinics, volunteer groups and family businesses. Pick: Staff or volunteers: shifts, hours, handovers, approvals. Not a sports squad (sports)
- ticketing: Discover, compare, buy, present and resell passes for live shows, games or concerts, including seat prices and mobile ticket wallets. Pick: Use ticketing alone for discovering nearby concerts, comparing seats and presenting passes. Near me is a search filter, not another job. Add places only for a separately requested venue directory, not for ticket listings or seat maps. Not organizing your own event (events), retail checkouts (commerce), or cinema showtimes (watch).
- trips: One trip from planning to coming home: the plan day by day, the confirmations for flights, trains, stays and tickets, what to pack, the documents to carry, the weather where you are going, money in the local currency and the time back home. Shared costs on a trip come from money; places to visit from places. Pick: Trip planning or a travel wallet: itineraries, existing travel confirmations, packing, passport and visa expiry, destination forecasts. Those travel details do not also need booking, paperwork or places. Not organising an event (events)
- utilities: Everyday device tools: scientific calculators, unit converters, language translation, QR studios, network speed testing and device file management. Pick: Pick even for one dedicated tool: generate or scan QR codes, or browse device folders, inspect storage and move files into a locked local folder. Not account protection (security), trip-only currency references (trips), an AI workspace (assistant), or shared cloud folders (workspace).
- watch: Television, film and cinema: multi-season catalogs, live TV guides, resume queues, TV remotes, cinema showtimes and auditorium seat selection. Pick: Use for watching a video catalog, controlling a TV or picking a cinema showing. Not audio or prose libraries (media), live non-cinema ticket markets (ticketing), or playing one local recording (core).
- weather: Dedicated forecasts and conditions: hourly curves, daily temperature ranges, air quality, UV, pollen, severe alerts, sun and moon arcs, saved cities and radar snapshots. Pick: Only choose for actual weather, air-quality or astronomical conditions, not a daily schedule or a statistics chart. Not weather as one detail of a trip itinerary (trips), or venue discovery (places).
- workspace: Shared cloud files and folders, quick notes, versioned team wikis and document review with link and role permissions. Pick: Use when people organize or collaborate on cloud documents or structured wiki pages. Not local files (utilities), personal life-admin records (paperwork), or published books (media).

Idea: Find a place for a weekend away. Compare nightly prices on a date calendar, see room rate options and refund rules, and watch for price drops.
Reply with a JSON array of up to 3 pack ids, or [] when none fit.

- money: Personal and household money: what is in each account, where it went, what is due, who owes whom, how to clear debts, and how a holding is doing.
